name: Closing Wire Fraud
description: Fraudsters inside a compromised transaction thread send buyers altered wiring instructions days before closing, diverting down payments and payoff wires.
assumptions: Attempts track transaction volume; listing data makes closing dates public.
Primary loss reflects the brokerage's share of unrecovered funds and settlements.
Secondary loss covers litigation over duty of care and reputational damage in the market.

name: Tenant Application Data Breach
description: An intrusion into property management systems exposes tenant applications — SSNs, income documents, and background screening results.
assumptions: Retention of years of applications multiplies exposed records beyond current tenants.
Primary loss covers forensics, notification, and credit monitoring.
Secondary loss covers state privacy enforcement and class-action exposure.

name: Ransomware Hits Property Operations
description: Ransomware encrypts property management and accounting systems; rent processing, maintenance dispatch, and owner statements stall during rebuild.
assumptions: Rent obligations survive the outage; the loss is processing delay and rebuild labor.
Backups restore within a week; no ransom payment is modeled.
Secondary loss covers owner-client attrition and trust-account audit costs.

name: Smart Building Systems Compromise
description: Attackers reach networked access control, HVAC, and elevator systems across managed commercial properties, disrupting building operations.
asset: Building automation and access control systems
assumptions: Life-safety systems fail safe; the loss is disruption, manual staffing, and re-securing.
Vendor remote-access accounts are the assumed entry path.
Secondary loss covers tenant SLA claims and lease-renewal friction.

name: Agent Email Account Takeovers
description: Phishing takes over agent mailboxes, seeding future closing fraud and exposing client financial documents circulating in transactions.
assumptions: Independent-contractor agents on personal devices raise both frequency and vulnerability.
Primary loss covers response, client notification, and monitoring per takeover.
Secondary loss captures takeovers that seed later wire fraud, modeled separately.
